clue.text: The fence is quite dim about 1 down

annotationWithheld.why: The fence is quite dim about 1 down (8): PALE (quite dim) round IS + AD fits, but 1 down (POLISH) gives no AD; the cross-reference looks misprinted or misread and no source gives the clue as printed
annotationWithheld.clue: The fence is quite dim about 1 down

clue.text: East European sophistication

definitions.meaning: from Poland, a country in eastern Europe

explanation.definitionFit: Polish describes things from Poland; polish, with a small p, is refinement of manner or style.

clue.text: Switched-on track suit

parts.note: a live circuit is switched on, carrying current
RY is short for railway, a railway track

explanation.surface: A trendy, up-to-the-minute tracksuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Track suit' reads as sportswear; the words split, 'track' giving the railway and 'suit' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Livery is the distinctive uniform worn by servants or members of a guild, a suit of clothes in a set style.

clue.text: Call hikers crazy

indicators.note: crazy suggests the letters of hikers going wild into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone shouts at a group of walkers that they're mad.
explanation.definitionFit: A shriek is a high piercing cry, a kind of call.

clue.text: Base of French groups, note

parts.note: de is the French word for of
genera are biological groupings of species
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: French factions form the foundation of a short message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Base' looks like a noun for a foundation; it is the adjective meaning low or depraved.
explanation.definitionFit: Base and degenerate both describe someone morally low and corrupt.

clue.text: Sceptically request a social worker

parts.note: to request something is to ask for it
the ant is the classic social insect, and most ants are workers

explanation.surface: Someone eyes a request to see a council social worker with suspicion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' looks like a council employee; here it is the ant, an insect living in colonies.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking askant, or askance, is eyeing something with doubt or mistrust, which is how a sceptic looks.

clue.text: Hardened, so needs a new treatment

indicators.note: giving the letters of so needs a a new treatment rearranges them

explanation.surface: Something already toughened up still requires a fresh approach.
explanation.definitionFit: Seasoned timber or troops have been hardened by time and exposure.

clue.text: Reluctance to provide a translation

parts.note: a version is a rendering of a text in another language

explanation.surface: A translator is unwilling to take on the job.
explanation.definitionFit: An aversion is a strong dislike or disinclination, the feeling behind unwillingness.

clue.text: Court official introducing counsel to man

indicators.note: introducing puts the counsel piece first, leading into the man piece

parts.note: a tip is a piece of advice or counsel
to man a place is to staff it

explanation.surface: A court officer brings a barrister in to meet a client.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counsel' suggests a barrister in court; here it is advice, and 'man' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipstaff is a sheriff's officer or court usher who carries out the court's orders.

clue.text: Left always ahead of time such an advantage

indicators.note: ahead of places the left-and-always pieces in front of the time piece

parts.note: ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Being left-handed always gives a player a head start: that's the edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Leverage is power or influence that gives one side the upper hand, a kind of edge.

clue.text: Form and face applied

definitions.meaning: one's composition or character, as in 'it is in his nature'

explanation.definitionFit: Make-up is both a thing's constitution (its form) and the cosmetics worn on the face.

clue.text: The impulse in boys to become doctors

indicators.note: in places the impulse word inside the word for boys

parts.note: sons are boys of a family
an urge is a sudden impulse

explanation.surface: A sudden urge leads some lads to train in medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgeons are medical practitioners who operate, so they are doctors of a kind.

clue.text: A county's constituents sorted out

indicators.note: constituents are the parts or letters making up the word sorted, which are to be dealt with
sorted out means put into a fresh arrangement, so those letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Voters in a shire find their grievances dealt with by the local council.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constituents' suggests voters in a constituency; it means the letters that make up 'sorted', which 'out' tells you to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorset is a county on the south coast of England.

clue.text: Motorists want them — but not about their person!

definitions.text: Motorists want them — but not about their person!

parts.words: Motorists want them — but not about their person!
parts.note: drivers need a reserve wheel in the boot, but nobody wants the same-named roll of fat round the waist

explanation.definitionFit: Spare tyres are reserve wheels carried in a car, and also a slang term for flab around the midriff.

clue.text: Allowed to alight, but declined

definitions.meaning: let out of a car or bus at a stop
fell away or dwindled, as numbers or interest do

explanation.definitionFit: A passenger let out at the kerb has been set down; a figure that fell has dwindled, the same phrase in each sense.

clue.text: Anybody wanting air pants in order to get it

indicators.note: putting the letters of air pants in order rearranges them

explanation.surface: Someone after a pair of breezy trousers must queue for them.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspirant is someone who aspires, who seeks or hopes for a goal.

clue.text: A book about lubricants involving much work

indicators.note: about means the book word goes round the lubricants word

parts.note: a tome is a book, usually a large one
oils are used as lubricants

explanation.surface: A manual on engine lubrication is heavy going.
explanation.definitionFit: Toilsome means laborious, demanding great effort.

clue.text: Flag, as usual

definitions.meaning: normal, regular, supplied as a matter of course

explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a banner carried in battle; standard also means normal or customary.

clue.text: A little relation's summer wear — right on!

indicators.note: on places the right-wing piece after the clothing piece

parts.note: shorts are short trousers worn in warm weather
a Tory is a member of the right-wing UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A young relative's holiday outfit gets a cheer of approval: right on!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relation' looks like a relative; it means a narration or account, and a little one is brief fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: A relation is an account or narrative, and a brief prose tale is such an account on a small scale.

clue.text: Talk incessantly of overweight in the young child

indicators.note: in places the turned weight abbreviation inside the word for a young child

parts.note: a babe is a baby or infant

indicators.note: over tells you the weight abbreviation is turned round

parts.note: lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight

explanation.surface: Chattering on about an infant being too heavy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overweight' reads as one word; split it: 'over' turns LB into BL, which 'in' puts inside BABE.
explanation.definitionFit: To babble is to chatter on and on, talking without pause.

clue.text: Capital investment for the saintly

parts.note: capital is used in the sense of the head, and investment in the sense of clothing: the headwear a holy figure wears in paintings

explanation.definitionFit: A nimbus is the halo of light painted round the head of a saint.

clue.text: A swinish trait that's generally accepted

parts.note: greed is the trait associated with pigs

explanation.surface: Everyone agrees that piggishness is a fault.
explanation.definitionFit: Something agreed has been settled by common consent, so it is accepted by all.

clue.text: In the money and upcountry

parts.note: L stands for the pound sterling, from Latin libra
taken as written

explanation.surface: Being rich and living out in the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Upcountry describes the interior of a land, away from the coast.

clue.text: Taking tea to occupy an armed supporter

indicators.note: to occupy means the tea word sits inside the supporter word

parts.note: a sling supports an injured arm, so it is a supporter for the arm
taken as written

explanation.surface: Bringing tea to a soldier who is guarding something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Armed supporter' suggests a gun-carrying backer; it is the sling for a broken arm.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealing is taking what belongs to someone else.

clue.text: A few love law-breaking. There's a frank confession

annotationWithheld.why: A few love law-breaking. There's a frank confession (6): A + V + O (love) + anagram of LAW gives AVOWAL only if 'few' supplies V; no parse of the clue as held gives the V, so a word looks misread and no source gives the printed clue
annotationWithheld.clue: A few love law-breaking. There's a frank confession

clue.text: The page may be dressed as expected

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for page
robable is a playful coinage meaning able to be robed, that is, fit to be dressed

explanation.surface: A court page may be dressed up for the occasion, as everyone anticipated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Robable' is not a dictionary word for 'can be robed'; the setter builds it from robe plus -able.
explanation.definitionFit: Something probable is likely, the outcome one would anticipate.

clue.text: Stylish attempt to encompass an objective

indicators.note: to encompass means the attempt word goes round the objective word

parts.note: a try is an attempt
an end is an aim or objective, as in 'to that end'

explanation.surface: A fashionable effort to take in a goal.
explanation.definitionFit: Trendy means fashionable, keeping up with the latest style.

clue.text: Like second letter newspaper leader rated

parts.note: as means like, as in 'as good as new'
ess is the spelt-out name of the letter S
the editor heads a newspaper, abbreviated ED

explanation.surface: A newspaper's editorial comment is graded like a letter to the editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Newspaper leader' looks like an editorial; it is the editor who leads the paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To assess is to evaluate or judge the worth of something, so rated means evaluated.
